newsitem.title: UK: Brokers GNI see wheat prices higher, corn down.
newsitem.headline: Brokers GNI see wheat prices higher, corn down.

text.p: Wheat has the potential to rise to $5.00 per bushel, while corn can be expected to fall to $2.50 soon, according to brokers GNI.
On Tuesday, May CBOT wheat closed at $4.11, while May corn closed at $2.91-1/2.

The new wheat crop has experienced a series of setbacks, GNI said in its Commodity Perspective report. It noted a severe freeze which hit winter wheat areas in southern Kansas, Oklahoma and the Texas panhandle, and concerns over the French crop following a prolonged dry spell.
"This leaves wheat even more likely to experience a supply deficit in the 1997/98 supply year," GNI said.

In contrast, "a massive world surplus of corn is on the way, which will push prices sharply lower," GNI said. Even so the brokerage expects traders to keep a close eye on France, although it is less important for corn than for wheat, and on other areas of western Europe.
The USDA world supply and demand report will be watched closely for wheat and corn, GNI said.
